line: Start with your projects. Add a folder once, and every agent, file, and conversation stays organized around it.
Then pick any agent: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and more, all from one composer. Let's ask for a pricing page.
The agent writes the page into your project, and the result opens right beside the conversation.
For bigger goals, just ask for a Squad. The agent launches it: an orchestrator plans the work and hands tasks to agents working in parallel.
Flow view shows how the work hands off, from the plan to the review, until the Squad is done.
And Zana is modular: everything beyond the core is a plugin. Add one from the marketplace, in one click.
Or install your own, straight from a folder. Here, our team's GUS plugin.
GUS opens as a panel with my sprint board: every ticket I'm working on.
Open a ticket, press Work with agent, and the agent starts with the whole ticket as context.
And because plugins are just code, an agent can change them too. Let's add a dashboard.
It edits the plugin, Zana rebuilds it, and the new Dashboard tab is live: tickets by status, the sprint countdown, and what's blocked.
To share it, just ask. The agent pushes it to your team's repository, and colleagues install it from Plugins.
And Zana goes where you go: the same app on your phone, with Slack on the way.
That's Zana: every agent, one command center.
